name: Beef Bourguignon Pot Pie

ingredients.name: neutral oil, such as vegetable, plus more as needed
dry red wine, such as Pinot Noir
puff pastry, from 1 frozen puff pastry thawed

instructions.primary_message: Cut the boneless beef chuck into 1 1/2-inch cubes. Finely dice the yellow onion. Mince the garlic. Cut the thick-cut bacon into 1/4-inch pieces. Trim and thinly slice the button mushrooms. Beat the egg.
instructions.secondary_message:
0.68 kg boneless beef chuck
1 small yellow onion
2 medium cloves garlic
2 slices thick-cut bacon
227 g button mushrooms
1 large egg

instructions.primary_message: In a large Dutch oven, heat oil over medium-high heat until shimmering. Pat beef dry with paper towels and sprinkle all over with salt and pepper. Cook half of beef until browned on all sides, 4 to 5 minutes, adjusting heat as necessary to avoid burning. Transfer browned beef to a plate, then repeat with remaining beef.

Add onion, diced carrots, garlic, and salt and pepper to Dutch oven, and cook, stirring occasionally, until beginning to brown, 5 to 7 minutes. (If bottom of pan begins to look overly brown, add a splash of water and use a wooden spoon to scrape fond from bottom of pan.)

Add flour and cook, stirring frequently to coat vegetables, until no dry flour remains and flour begins to turn golden, 1 to 2 minutes. Stir in tomato paste. Add wine, broth, soy sauce, thyme, bay leaf, and fish sauce (if using), stirring to incorporate. Bring liquid to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low.

Return beef to pot. Reduce heat to low, cover, and gently simmer, stirring occasionally, until beef is very tender and broth has thickened enough to coat the back of a spoon, 1 1/2 to 2 hours. (If broth seems watery, simmer, uncovered, until thickened, 5 to 10 minutes. Keep in mind that broth will continue to thicken in the oven. If broth seems too thick, add a small splash of water to thin it out.) Remove from heat; skim off excess fat, if desired.
Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 205°C (400°F).

Heat a 25-cm cast iron skillet over medium heat. Add bacon and cook, stirring occasionally, until fat has rendered and bacon is golden and crisp, about 7 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer bacon to stew. Discard all but 1 tablespoon of fat.

Increase the heat to medium-high and add the mushrooms to skillet with bacon fat. Cook, stirring occasionally until well-browned, about 10 minutes. Add remaining sliced carrots and cook until just tender and beginning to brown, 5 to 7 minutes more.
Pour stew into the cast iron skillet and mix to evenly incorporate vegetables. Let sit while you prepare the dough.

On a lightly floured surface, roll puff pastry sheet to an 28-cm square. Carefully place on top of beef filling; fold excess dough underneath itself and crimp as desired just below rim of skillet so it's flush with the skillet's edge. Using a sharp paring knife, cut three small slits into top of pastry. Using a pastry brush, lightly brush dough with beaten egg.
Bake until pastry is puffed, golden brown, and crisp, 20 to 25 minutes. Let cool for 5 minutes before serving.

description: The easiest way to upgrade this classic French stew? Turn it into a pot pie.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Dash of fish sauce (optional)

Optional substitutions: low-sodium chicken broth → beef broth; button mushrooms → cremini mushrooms

Make-ahead and storage: The stew can be made through step 4 up to 3 days in advance. Once cool, refrigerate in an airtight container. When ready to assemble, proceed with step 5.
This pot pie is best enjoyed the day it’s made. Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 3 days.
author: Zola Gregory
